steps.tx: **Bartter syndrome** is an autosomal recessive salt-wasting tubulopathy of the thick ascending limb caused by mutations in NKCC2 (Type **1**, **SLC12A1**), ROMK (Type **2**, KCNJ1), **CLC-Kb** (Type **3**, CLCNKB), or **barttin** (Type **4**, BSND with sensorineural deafness), while Type **5** involves MAGED2.

vis.caption: Solute transporter pathways and inherited genetic defects in tubulopathies. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Bartter syndrome manifests with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, **hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism**, **normal-to-low blood pressure**, marked **hypercalciuria**, and early medullary **nephrocalcinosis**. Elevated urinary prostaglandin E2 is common, and early indomethacin therapy provides significant clinical improvement in affected infants. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Gitelman syndrome** is an autosomal recessive tubulopathy caused by loss-of-function mutations in **SLC12A3** encoding the thiazide-sensitive **NCC** cotransporter in the **distal convoluted tubule**, typically presenting during adolescence or adult life with fatigue. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Gitelman syndrome** is clinically distinguished from Bartter syndrome by prominent **hypocalciuria** with urine calcium-to-creatinine ratio under **0.20** mg/mg or **0.05** mmol/mmol, accompanied by severe refractory **hypomagnesemia** without medullary nephrocalcinosis. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

right.title: Bartter Syndrome
points: Affected site: Thick ascending limb (NKCC2 / ROMK)

steps.tx: **Liddle syndrome** is an autosomal dominant condition caused by gain-of-function mutations in the **PY motif** of the beta or gamma subunits of **ENaC**, preventing binding by **NEDD4-2** ubiquitin ligase and abolishing normal channel endocytosis. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Liddle syndrome** manifests as severe early-onset hypertension with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, suppressed plasma renin activity, and undetectable aldosterone, termed **pseudoaldosteronism**. It responds selectively to ENaC blockers **amiloride** or **triamterene**, whereas spironolactone is completely ineffective. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Pseudohypoaldosteronism** type **1**, or **PHA1**, presents with salt wasting, hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis, and high aldosterone. Autosomal dominant PHA1 involves the mineralocorticoid receptor gene **NR3C2**, whereas recessive PHA1 involves loss-of-function **ENaC** mutations. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Autosomal Dominant PHA1
points: Gene defect: Inactivating mutation in NR3C2
Organ involvement: Restricted exclusively to renal tubules
Prognosis: Improves spontaneously with advancing age

right.title: Autosomal Recessive PHA1
points: Gene defect: Loss-of-function mutations in ENaC subunits
Organ involvement: Systemic (colon, lungs, sweat glands, kidneys)
Severity: Life-threatening neonatal hyperkalemic salt crisis
Prognosis: Lifelong severe salt repletion requirement

steps.tx: **Gordon syndrome**, termed pseudohypoaldosteronism type **2** or familial hyperkalemic hypertension, is caused by mutations in **WNK4**, **WNK1**, **CUL3**, or **KLHL3**, driving constitutive activation of NCC and responding rapidly to low-dose **thiazide** diuretics. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
